paragraph: Bergenfield is a single-family town, and the data leaves little room for interpretation. Sixty-seven homes sold over six months at a median of $699,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.045, roughly 75 percent of homes closing above asking, and a median of 19 days on market. That is a real seller's market, with plenty of multiple offer situations behind those numbers. The spread runs from $395,000 to $1,750,000, so the median is the better guide than the average here. Multi-family is a small but real second tier, six sales at a median of $745,000 with a ratio slightly under list, which tells you investor buyers are negotiating in a way owner-occupant buyers are not. Condo and townhouse activity is effectively nonexistent, one sale in six months. On seasonality, June peaked at a $812,500 median on 12 closings and July came in at $650,000 on 15. Volume rose while the median fell, so read that as a mix shift toward entry-level product, not softening values. If the usual Bergen County arc holds, expect closings to thin out through fall while competition on well-priced homes stays firm.
